title: Charlie Parker drives wildly down 59th Street
summary: Butler first heard Parker live in the 1930s; later Parker took him in his car at 60 mph and ran up on a policeman near Columbus Circle before dropping him at Broadway.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: So, when did you first hear Parker live?
Well, I heard Parker live, let's see, in the '30's.
Oh, when he was still at the --

He was eating people up then. Then I lost track of him because I went to -- and the last time I saw him, we were, he had his automobile and he said, come on with me, he said, Jacques, I haven't seen you in a long time, come on with me -- and this was when I come back, I think it was -- let's see, I can't get the real date. I don't know because it -- can't pinpoint it.
But Parker took me in his automobile and said I'm going to drive you, I want you to go somewhere with me because I've got to get straight.

And I got in the automobile and we were on 59th Street and Charlie Parker put this car and ran 60 miles an hour, you know where the Bolivia statue is up there on 59th Street, and there was a big policeman standing there and Charlie Parker -- (verbally demonstrating) -- ran right up to the man, about a foot from the man and laughed. "Hey, M.F.!" What are you doing? And the man was so astounded, and I said, and that man -- my nerves, he was liable to put both of us away.
Says, go on, get on, get on, get on. I say, Charles, I think I'd better get off at Broadway because I got to go and get my music, you don't mind, do you?
No, no, but now, you come back because I'm having a party for my birthday.
